title: Grateful Dead Live at Dance Hall on 1967-09-04

ai_review.summary: Soundboard source with a rustic but listenable splice‑filled tape that captures a vivid Caution > Feedback jam bursting with psychedelic energy.
ai_review.review: The partial soundboard recording is generally clear, though the opening splice and a slightly rustic texture are noticeable.  Listeners rave about the extended Caution/Feedback improvisation – an early taste of the band’s Anthem‑of‑the‑Sun evolution – and the historic moment when Mickey Hart sat in for the first time, prompting Jerry to proclaim “THIS is the Grateful Dead.”

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the show highly (4‑5 stars) and praise the standout jam, while recording comments note only minor imperfections; the weighted assessment yields a strong overall score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Tape splice audible at the start; sound is a bit rustic but fully listenable. No major drop‑outs, though one reviewer noted set‑list mismatches.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The excerpt focuses on an experimental jam that showcases the band’s shift toward more complex, psychedelic compositions of the late ’60s.

band_member_comments.Jerry: After the show Jerry hugged Mickey and declared “THIS is the Grateful Dead,” underscoring his excitement about the performance.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass work is highlighted in recollections of the Caution/Feedback jam and his note that Mickey sat in toward the end.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey Hart makes his first appearance on drums late in the set, adding a new rhythmic dimension.
